components: Compare uniform permutation recurrence with a nonuniform absorbing-walk preparation whose phase shift and final threshold are supplied separately.

Compare a cosine-weighted hemisphere, midpoint-stopped odd-dimensional cube walks and cyclic ballot tapes with unbiased choices and sign detectors. The tape's herald is fixed before choosing the analyzer.

On eight supplied cube preparations, vertex, one-bit and erased-coordinate edge records have distinct information even when binary tests agree. The edge decoder uses the whole measurement; conditional no-click agreement is not normalized raw agreement.
candidates.declared_status: Conditional preparation and finite readout comparisons, not a new sphere model, derivation of the qubit rule, or selection of the physical carrier. A table mismatch applies only to the stated record and target.
missing_bridges: Derive a physical preparation with available settings, unbiased choices and registered herald or loss accounting; the sphere fixture starts from the supplied density.
Specify retained records and apparatus response for arbitrary states, sequential measurements and composite systems without importing the target rules.

Replay: `python3 -m unittest tests.test_preparation_candidate_probes`.
These are deterministic comparisons between mechanisms, not a fit to lab
data or a formal derivation. They target the phase settings missing from
the [two-setting hidden-mode tests](HIDDEN_MODE_CANDIDATES.md). None of
the following preparation protocols is synthesized from that native gate.

### Uniform recurrence is not a phase law

In the [phase-return probe](probe_phase_return_walk.py), start uniformly
in a finite bright set S, apply the same reversible permutation P each
time and read whether the state is still in S. The dark fraction after k
steps is the size of the symmetric difference of S and PᵏS, divided by
twice the size of S. The triangle inequality implies dark(2) ≤ 2 dark(1).
For the six-setting target (0,1/4,3/4,1,3/4,1/4) this forces a maximum
probability error of at least 1/12; a six-cycle attains the bound. It is
not a general exclusion of classical return sets: starting the same cycle
with weights (1,2,1) instead of (1,1,1) gives the target exactly.

One origin for these weights uses equal-probability left/right steps from
the odd sites of an interval with absorbing ends 0 and 2d. Check for
absorption at **each** step; observe survivors after an even number of
steps. The phase interface identifies the d surviving odd sites with
consecutive bins of a 2d-cycle. It supplies the shift and the final
threshold; these are not consequences of the preparation walk.

### Same probabilities, different preparations

| Carrier | Supplied rule | What is checked | Distinguishing control |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Unit sphere](probe_hemisphere_candidate.py) | Cosine-weighted preparation on one hemisphere; sign detector | Numerical quadrature of (1+n·m)/2, including nonaligned directions | Uniform hemisphere gives 1−angle/π; passive sequential ++ distinguishes mixtures that have identical single-sign statistics |
| [Odd-dimensional bit cube](probe_mid_edge_majority_walk.py) | Uniform adjacent edge, stop at the zero-score midpoint, then choose an endpoint; sign detector | Positive eigenvector (n·v)₊; all 64 direction pairs at d=3 and 1,024 at d=5 | Checking only the endpoint changes the d=3 center probability from 1/2 to 1/3; finite d=5 one-block readout is 19/25 rather than 4/5 |
| [Cyclic ballot tape](probe_cyclic_ballot_preparation.py) | Fair word v, independent uniform reading origin, increment ±1 for agreement/disagreement with preparation word n; stop at the first nonpositive prefix | For each word, exactly (n·v)₊ indexed rotations survive. Same endpoint weights without a long-time limit | Fixing the reading origin introduces a coordinate bias even when the total preparation yield is unchanged |

On the sphere the prepared density is proportional to (n·λ)₊. One
candidate mechanism is supplied isotropic diffusion killed at the equator:
n·λ is positive inside its hemisphere, vanishes on the boundary and is a
principal Dirichlet mode. The numerical fixture starts with that density;
it does **not** simulate or prove diffusion convergence. Splitting the
positive part into an absolute value and a linear term and integrating
over the detector hemisphere gives (1+n·m)/2 in every dimension ≥2.
Thus the law alone does not select the Bloch dimension. In three dimensions
this preparation and detector are the known qubit model of Kochen and
Specker, not a new physical proposal; see section “The Kochen-Specker
model” in [Harrigan and Spekkens](https://arxiv.org/abs/0706.2661).
The sphere fixture states its numerical tolerance and which tests reduce
the angular integral rather than sampling the full higher-dimensional sphere.

On an odd-dimensional bit cube, n,v,m have ±1 entries and the benchmark
is (1+n·m/d)/2; only the finite vertex directions are tested. Readout is
by majority of matches. One midpoint block from the uniform bright half
at d=3 has survival 1/2 and conditional masses (3,1,1,1)/6. On the tape
the same endpoint distribution comes from an initially **unrestricted**
cube, with exact herald fraction 1/4 at d=3, 3/16 at d=5, 5/32 at d=7.
Here the herald is determined by preparation before the analyzer is
chosen. It is not permission to discard later detector failures.

All three constructions assume the available settings, source of
unbiased choices, and a way to read a sign. They neither select the
primitive nor derive arbitrary measurements, composite systems, Pauli
statistics or physical scales. An experiment that distinguishes two
preparations must also specify what is retained between measurements.

Replay: `python3 -m unittest tests.test_cube_detector_probes`. A source
setting is a word n of three signs. As a comparison with a qubit, assign
it the **supplied** Bloch direction n/√3. The original eight sign tests
use directions of this same form. The comparison below varies the record
retained by the source, while keeping the apparatus independent of n
given the received record. No statistics in this file are experimental
data or a derivation of the qubit measurement rule.

| Record delivered | Eight cube-aligned binary tests | Matching four-outcome tetrahedral apparatus | One new orientation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Final vertex v of the [preparation](PREPARATION_CANDIDATES.md), law (n·v)₊/6 | All reproduced by majority | Best normalized worst-entry error 1/24 | Face diagonal separates two preparations |
| Uniformly chosen coordinate and its single bit | All reproduced by comparing that bit | All reproduced: pick uniformly one of the two tetrahedron words matching the bit | Cartesian coordinate reveals a strict information limit |
| Uniformly chosen erased coordinate and the two surviving bits (an edge) | All reproduced | Reproduced, including rotated tetrahedra | Enough for each finite-outcome qubit measurement on these eight source settings |

### A genuinely normalized measurement

The four target effects use tetrahedral sign words tⱼ of parity +1, with
p(j|n)=(1+n·tⱼ/3)/4. This is one device returning one of four outcomes,
not four separate yes/no tests with independent denominators. For the
quantum benchmark see [Renes et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0310075).

The [endpoint certificate](probe_endpoint_tetra_detector.py) permits *any*
stochastic four-outcome detector on v, not just threshold detectors. Let
D± denote the mean, over j, of its reported P(j|±tⱼ). Normalization at
each hidden vertex gives D+ + 3D− ≥ 2/3, whereas the ideal table gives
1/2. A detector with maximum entry error 1/24 attains the lower bound.
Using only four negative preparations and one positive still separates,
with exact error 1/52. All six ways to merge a pair of outcomes admit
normalized response functions. Reject only the specified unrefined
carrier and target, not all vertex models or all binary tests.

An apparatus with an extra no-click outcome can reproduce the **conditional**
four-outcome table at efficiency 2/3 for *every* preparation. The fixture
checks the raw losses and the ceiling under exact conditional agreement
and common efficiency. In a separate two-outcome test the target contrast
between words (+++) and (--+) along (1,1,0)/√2 is √(2/3), whereas their
endpoint distributions have total variation 2/3. Any source-independent
readout can only reduce that distance.

For qubit effects specified by weights aⱼ and vectors rⱼ, the supplied
formula has gⱼ=aⱼrⱼ/√3, Σaⱼ=1, Σaⱼrⱼ=0 and |rⱼ|≤1. Each demand is at
most 1/√3, below 2/3. In contrast, a target that copies one coordinate
with certainty exceeds capacity. The one-bit channel's corresponding
capacity for a single coordinate is just 1/3.

The edge decoder is constructed from the whole requested measurement.
It is not an apparatus-independent representation of each effect, not an
origin for arbitrary physical settings, and not a sequential measurement
or composition law. These models agree on a substantial family of tests
but retain different latent information. Passing the eight preparations
does not establish a model for all qubit states.
